q:
A student writes every program using only `while True:` loops with `break`, and long chains of separate `if` statements instead of `elif`.

Discuss the readability, correctness and maintenance consequences of this style, compared with using the most appropriate construct. (6)
ms: Level-marked. while True hides the real stopping condition — readers must hunt for breaks; risk of missed/never-reached break = infinite loop; count-controlled cases are clearer/safer as for-range. Separate ifs are all evaluated: slower, and multiple branches can fire when only one was intended (grade-band bugs); elif documents mutual exclusivity and stops at the first match. Appropriate constructs make intent visible, ease testing/maintenance, reduce bugs. Balanced answers may note while True + break is legitimate for at-least-once input validation. 5–6: several developed consequences with examples and a balanced conclusion; 3–4: some valid points; 1–2: basic.
